proof.criterion: After a broker outage longer than a pod's lease, a Legion pod fetches a secret again within one renewal interval of the broker serving again, with no relaunch and no person acting
proof.surface: the real broker binary run twice on one real Postgres 16.4 database, the real agent-secrets binary (keygen, renew --pod-token-file, NAME -- cmd) as the worker shim runs it, a test-owned TCP forwarder holding one address across the restart; lease 45 s, sweep 1 s, drain 0
proof.observed: survivor held 39.947s at the stop; second broker listened 58.088s after the first exited; survivor's first CLI fetch served 78ms after listening; its renewer (never exited) renewed to 44.924s past now 5.968s after listening; broker logged 'INFO broker: gave back the time no broker was serving ... gap=58.307957s ... enrollments=2'; --- PASS (83.84s); 0 '--- SKIP'
proof.negativeControl: the same outage_test.go in a git-archive export of eee16056's packages/envoy, GOWORK=off: --- FAIL (77.75s) at step (1), 'agent-secrets: proof invalid: not live (PROOF_INVALID)', 0 skips

proof.criterion: An enrollment that was really ended stays ended: revoked, lapsed while a broker served, or renewed with another pod's or service account's token
proof.surface: the same real-binary run after the restart
proof.observed: revoked pod (launcher DELETE) and lapsed pod (ended by the first broker's sweeper) each refused fetch 401 PROOF_INVALID 'not live' and renew 401 ENROLLMENT_NOT_LIVE; the mismatch pod's renewal with a token naming another pod UID and with another service account each refused 403 POD_IDENTITY_MISMATCH, its lease_expires_at unchanged
proof.negativeControl: renewing the survivor with its own pod token after the restart succeeds (step 2), so the refusals are identity- and state-specific, not a broker that refuses everything

proof.criterion: The guard holds for a database outage while the broker process keeps running, and under concurrent beats
proof.surface: in-process broker services on real Postgres
proof.observed: all ok (383 PASS, 0 SKIP at e53dda04; enroll and config re-run ok with 0 SKIP at 8f8b7ddb); TestAPodWhoseLeaseRanOutWhileNoBrokerServedRenewsAndReadsItsGrant: stale serving row, pod renews 200 and reads WORKER_TOKEN; TestTwoBeatsAtOnceGiveTheTimeBackOnce passes
proof.negativeControl: in the same api test, a pod whose lease ran out before the last beat is refused renew 401 ENROLLMENT_NOT_LIVE; TestBeforeAnyBeatALapsedLeaseIsLapsed shows the guard off with no threshold recorded

proof.criterion: The daemon logs in again within about 10 s of the broker answering
proof.surface: the daemon's broker client against an httptest broker that hijacks and closes login connections, then answers
proof.observed: TestTokenLoginRetriesQuicklyWhileTheBrokerDoesNotAnswer and TestTokenLoginRetriesSlowlyWhenTheBrokerRefuses PASS 5/5 (and 3/3 after the simplify pass)
proof.negativeControl: a broker answering 401 keeps the long schedule: the second login arrives no earlier than the long wait (TestTokenLoginRetriesSlowlyWhenTheBrokerRefuses)

trickyParts: The guard is a SQL function evaluated in the same statement as every lease read, so a request stalled on Postgres past the threshold answers as it would once the time was given back; only the beat locks broker_serving, so there is no lock cycle.
The beat reads clock_timestamp() only after taking the row lock, so a second concurrent beat sees the gap the first closed (time given back once).
outage_test.go uses only symbols present on eee16056 so it proves the failure there; it stops the broker between two survivor renewals so the given-back lease is distinguishable from a real renewal.
